plan_meta.name: Unified systems, coding and modern AI curriculum
plan_meta.intent: Basic ML and deep learning are theory: read, explain, diagram and calculate small examples. Projects use pretrained models and existing libraries. No required classical-model training, NumPy/PyTorch training lab, tiny transformer training or fine-tuning project.
plan_meta.schedule_rule: 140 undated study days across 20 weeks. Day 70 is an interview checkpoint; February 2027 is the planning horizon, with a flexible buffer.
non_guarantees: Day 70 is a readiness checkpoint, not an offer or role-level guarantee.
15 projects are learning opportunities, not 15 resume entries.
Dates are not assigned; preserve your actual start and progress.

candidate_profile.name: Your profile
candidate_profile.positioning: Customize this starter plan around your own evidence and target roles.

dsa_language_decision.exception: Practice the language required by a target role.
dsa_language_decision.rule: Explain invariants, complexity, and failure cases.

operating_rules.scope: Theory for basic ML/DL; modern pretrained-model integrations, evaluation, retrieval, bounded workflows and serving. No required foundational training, custom agent harness or new UI framework.
operating_rules.ownership: Work README describes team/Claude-assisted capabilities; distinguish designed, personally coded, AI-assisted and explainable work. Do not infer harness mastery.
operating_rules.overload: If 21 focused hours/week is not sustainable, extend the cycle. Drop companion DSA attempts and optional integration before sacrificing sleep; do not silently shrink practice and promise the same readiness.
operating_rules.ai_help: Unaided first attempt for interview problems and core project logic. Then hints, minimal reproductions and review. Separate assisted completion from independent recall.
operating_rules.revision: Due retries at +2,+7,+14 days are selected inside the daily DSA timebox; carry at most one blocked project task.

projects.name: Where did my disk space actually go?

Hard links versus copies; create disposable fixtures without touching the media library
Streaming hashes and grouping by size before hashing; compare two files
Walk errors, symlinks/reparse points and read-only scope; write boundary tests
Freeze scan scope and three acceptance checks; confirm permissions on fixtures
projects.build: Implement read-only traversal, file-identity grouping and candidate duplicate hashing; print a compact report.
projects.test: Test unique files, duplicates, hard links, unreadable entries and links outside the selected root; explain storage-estimation limits.
projects.proof: A runnable scanner, fixture tests and logical-size versus storage-estimate report.
projects.stop: No deletion, deduplication, automatic cleanup or whole-disk scan.

interview_curriculum.positioning: Software/backend and modern AI engineering; day70 readiness checkpoint with AI implementation depth continuing through February.
interview_curriculum.difficulty: 80 scheduled targets: 16 Easy, 52 Medium and 12 Hard. Six classic hard-pattern exercises replace medium slots; displaced mediums remain linked on the affected days as optional prerequisites. No repeat-frequency guarantee; master the pattern rather than memorize code.
interview_curriculum.question_policy: Use the existing 80 linked targets in the 60-minute weekday budget through day70; defer companion problems when needed. After day70, maintain weak patterns and mocks inside 30 minutes/day.

questions.title: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Remove Nth Node From End of List
Kth Smallest Element in a BST
Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
Kth Largest Element in an Array
Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

interview_curriculum.language: Python default for algorithm practice. Use Java for selected existing solutions and concurrency/LLD if targeting Java roles; do not solve everything twice.
readiness: Coding: over 3 separate mocks, independently solve an unseen medium-style task in 35-40 minutes with tests and complexity, plus explain a follow-up. This is our practice gate, not an employer cutoff.
Speed track: after correctness is stable, practise two appropriately sized questions in 45-55 minutes when the recruiter confirms that format; do not assume two hard questions.
Design: complete three 45-minute closed-book designs covering requirements, estimates, API/data model, bottlenecks, failure recovery, operations and security; explain alternatives.
Behavioral: six truthful stories covering ownership, conflict, failure, ambiguity, impact and learning; explain which code/design decisions were personally yours.
Applied AI: explain baseline versus model, eval labels/leakage, retrieval quality, inference limits and why an agent may be unnecessary.
interview_curriculum.scoring: Score 0-4 on correctness, approach/invariants, complexity/trade-offs, testing/failure analysis and communication. 16/20 with no zero in correctness is an internal green signal, never an offer prediction.
interview_curriculum.ddia_rule: Edition not assumed. First-edition chapter hints are labeled; use equivalent topic headings in second edition. Read selected sections, not whole chapters in a 20-minute slot. DDIA complements rather than replaces timed interview design.

learning_library.summary: A 20-week systems and modern AI path: interview readiness at day 70, deeper implementation through February.
learning_library.theory_policy: Basic ML and deep learning are theory: read, explain, diagram and calculate small examples. Projects use pretrained models and existing libraries. No required classical-model training, NumPy/PyTorch training lab, tiny transformer training or fine-tuning project.

resources.description: The main systems reference: storage, replication, transactions, streams and trade-offs. Read by topic; record the edition before assigning chapters.

resources.title: MIT 6.5840: Distributed Systems
resources.description: Deepen replication and fault-tolerance reasoning. Selected lectures and papers first; the full programming labs are a later commitment.

resources.title: Google SRE books
resources.description: SLOs, monitoring, overload and incident practice, with a practical workbook. Use one operational question per reading session.

resources.title: PostgreSQL documentation
resources.description: Indexes, query plans, concurrency, isolation and recovery. Match documentation to the installed major version.

resources.title: roadmap.sh: System Design
resources.description: A secondary coverage checklist for missing concepts and sequencing. It does not replace explanations or establish mastery.

resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
resources.description: Author-hosted mathematics text: vectors, decompositions, calculus, probability and optimization. Study only the prerequisites a current topic needs.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
resources.description: Practical tokenizer, model, dataset and fine-tuning workflows. Reading is free; some training exercises need compute.

resources.title: Stanford CS224N public archive
resources.description: NLP and neural-model foundations with public slides and assignments. Use selected lectures; self-study does not include staff feedback.

resources.title: vLLM documentation
resources.description: Serving, batching, KV-cache behavior and deployment. Read implementation details after measurement fundamentals; verify hardware support before running.

resources.title: roadmap.sh: AI Engineer
resources.description: Cross-check applied-AI topics absent from a research-oriented sequence, particularly application integration and evaluation.

resources.title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
resources.description: Processes, concurrency and persistence. Start with files, threads and crash behavior; link to author-hosted chapters instead of mirroring them.

resources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
resources.description: Consult methods, status codes, safe operations and idempotency when specifying APIs. A reference to look up, not a sequential assignment.

resources.title: Use The Index, Luke!
resources.description: Author-written practical SQL indexing. Pair predicates and index order with your own query plans.

resources.title: PostgreSQL: Transaction Isolation
resources.description: Reproduce an interleaving in two sessions. Record the database version and serialization retry behavior.

resources.title: RabbitMQ: Acknowledgements and Confirms
resources.description: Separate publisher confirmation, consumer acknowledgement and committed application effects. Start with crash timelines.

resources.title: Introduction to Information Retrieval
resources.description: Author/university-hosted text on postings, indexing, scoring and evaluation. A durable foundation for search experiments.

resources.title: AWS: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
resources.description: Practical reliability reading on retry amplification, deadlines and jitter. Official PDF fallback for the redirected article landing page.

resources.title: Dynamo: Amazon’s Highly Available Key-value Store
resources.description: Availability, partitioning, replication and conflict handling. Historical paper, not a specification of current DynamoDB.

resources.title: roadmap.sh: Backend Developer
resources.description: Check broad backend coverage. Some linked products or separate lesson packs can be paid; verify each assigned destination.

resources.title: Stanford CS229 public notes
resources.description: Regression, loss, regularization and statistical learning. This direct public PDF is distinct from the current course’s restricted materials.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
resources.description: Free interactive text and notebooks for tensors, differentiation, training and attention. Select small CPU examples.

resources.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
resources.description: Raschka’s official code is free; the full book is a library/purchase item. Useful for tiny attention and architecture implementations.

resources.title: AI Engineering — Chip Huyen
resources.description: Use the library book for evaluation, retrieval, adaptation and application trade-offs. The free companion contains supporting resources, not the full book.

resources.title: Designing Machine Learning Systems — Chip Huyen
resources.description: Data quality, deployment, monitoring and changing distributions. Library book plus free companion; read selectively around projects.

resources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
resources.description: Retrieval-generation motivation and experimental comparison. Distinguish the original trained architecture from application-level RAG pipelines.

resources.title: Ragas documentation
resources.description: Evaluation tooling after a manually labeled fixture exists. Model-based scoring can incur provider costs and needs human spot checks.

resources.title: vLLM benchmarking
resources.description: Workload and latency/throughput measurement for supported serving setups. Execution is elective until hardware compatibility is established.

resources.title: PagedAttention
resources.description: Primary paper for KV-cache block management and serving throughput. Read after attention, memory accounting and batching basics.

resources.title: llama.cpp
resources.description: CPU or supported hybrid inference. Model weights have separate licenses and memory requirements; begin with an available small model.

resources.title: MLflow for ML Models
resources.description: Track small local experiments, configurations and artifacts. Initial practice does not require hosted infrastructure.

resources.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): server concepts
resources.description: Official distinctions between tools, resources and prompts, with discovery/call/read operations and application control. Pair with the official SDK matching the chosen language; record protocol and SDK versions before building.

resources.title: LangGraph: persistence
resources.description: Official explanation of thread checkpoints, stores and recovery. For a local restart exercise use persistent storage, not an in-memory saver. Framework use is optional when a small explicit state machine fits the project budget.

resources.title: Hugging Face: image-text-to-text inference
resources.description: Official pretrained vision-language inference guide with image/text inputs and processor/model flow. Study the inference path; choose a model compatible with available memory and hardware rather than copying hardware-specific acceleration settings.

resources.title: How to Read a Paper - S. Keshav
resources.description: A short primary guide to staged paper reading and evaluating assumptions, evidence and related work; supports paper summaries across the AI curriculum.

resources.title: OWASP REST Security Cheat Sheet
resources.description: Fills the practical authz, object-scope, method and request-boundary gap for the read-only API/MCP projects; use selected sections with fixture identities.

resources.title: RFC 6455: The WebSocket Protocol
resources.description: Primary protocol source for the W7 connection-lifecycle topic; read the handshake, framing and close sections only.

resources.title: OpenTelemetry Signals
resources.description: Free primary project documentation that distinguishes traces, metrics and logs for SLOs and inference request traces.

resources.title: Redis Cache-Aside
resources.description: Official documentation gives an independent worked cache-aside example with TTLs, invalidation and stampede behavior for W4; use the pattern conceptually without requiring Redis setup.

resources.title: Redis Probabilistic Data Structures
resources.description: Official docs directly cover HyperLogLog, Count-Min Sketch, Top-K and t-digest, which are otherwise missing from the current source library; calculations can use supplied examples without deploying Redis.

resources.title: Hugging Face Transformers Generation Strategies
resources.description: Official current documentation distinguishes greedy/sampling/beam and advanced decoding; assign basic concepts only, with no custom generation code.

resources.title: OWASP LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
resources.description: Current primary security guidance for untrusted retrieval/tool outputs and fixture-based boundary checks in the RAG, MCP and agent work.
resources.review_topic: Prompt injection and tool trust boundaries

resources.title: TensorRT-LLM User Guide
resources.description: Official reference for quantization, batching and runtime concepts if compatible NVIDIA hardware exists; keep setup and GPU implementation elective.

resources.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
resources.description: Primary research paper for the optional reinforcement-learning module; extract objective, baselines and limits without reproducing or training a policy.

resources.description: Existing coding practice reference; evidence comes from independent attempts.

strands.title: Requirements and quantitative design
strands.subtext: Users, invariants, request rates, storage growth, latency budgets and explicit trade-offs. Produce a small design brief before choosing infrastructure.

strands.title: APIs, networking and request behavior
strands.subtext: Contracts, HTTP/gRPC choices, load balancing, timeouts, retries, idempotency, backpressure and overload. Trace one request through success and failure.

strands.title: Data models and transactional SQL
strands.subtext: Keys, normalization, indexes, query plans, isolation, locking, MVCC and migrations. Explain the correctness boundary as well as the fast path.

strands.title: Partitions, identities and caching
strands.subtext: Hot keys, partition boundaries, generated IDs, cache policy, staleness and invalidation. Use workload evidence to choose a design.

strands.title: Coordination and storage internals
strands.subtext: Replication, ordering, consensus, leases, fencing, WAL, B-trees, LSM trees and compaction. Deep implementation remains elective.

strands.title: Queues, streams and background work
strands.subtext: Delivery semantics, deduplication, consumer offsets, retries, lag, workflow boundaries and recovery. Separate task queues from replayable logs.

strands.title: Retrieval, ranking and compact analytics
strands.subtext: Inverted indexes, lexical ranking, hybrid retrieval, relevance metrics, sketches and approximate counts. Link directly to the retrieval projects.

strands.title: Product and media architectures
strands.subtext: Feeds, chat, notifications, geo queries, recommendations, uploads, transcoding, CDN and file sync. Select one walkthrough instead of building every product.

strands.title: Reliability, security and operating cost
strands.subtext: SLIs/SLOs, observability, restores, incident response, tenant boundaries, abuse controls, safe rollout and unit economics.

strands.title: Company cases and design interviews
strands.subtext: Read first-party architecture or incident accounts; distinguish the published workload from your own requirements. Explain why a simpler design might suffice.

strands.title: Evaluation before model complexity
strands.subtext: Baselines, development/test boundaries, leakage, metrics, calibration, error slices and uncertainty. Apply the theory to structured-output evaluation and pretrained semantic routing.

strands.title: Tensors, differentiation and neural models
strands.subtext: Theory: shapes, matrix products, gradients, chain rule, backpropagation and what a training loop does. Explain diagrams and small calculations; no training implementation is assigned.

strands.title: Tokens, attention and language models
strands.subtext: Theory of tokenization, embeddings, attention, positional information, normalization, loss and generation. Trace diagrams and small numerical examples; use pretrained models in projects.

strands.title: Retrieval and grounded applications
strands.subtext: Chunking, metadata filters, lexical versus vector search, reranking, citations, unsupported answers and retrieval evaluation.

strands.title: Structured outputs and bounded tools
strands.subtext: Validate output shape, meaning, authorization and side effects separately. Prefer deterministic code when it solves the task; compare an agent against that baseline.

strands.title: Adaptation and ML operations
strands.subtext: Dataset preparation, LoRA concepts, experiment/data versions, packaging, deployment, monitoring and rollback. No mandatory cloud cluster.

strands.title: Research and reinforcement learning
strands.subtext: Read a paper through its hypothesis, baselines and limitations. Policy gradients, PPO/GRPO and reproduction are optional depth paths, not prerequisites for the first job-prep cycle.

strands.title: Sets, logic and notation
strands.subtext: Translate statements, quantifiers, set operations and function notation into small examples. Skip only after an explanation check.

strands.title: Linear algebra for data and models
strands.subtext: Linear systems, spaces, bases, projections, spectra, low-rank approximation, least squares and PCA. Connect geometry to actual arrays.

strands.title: Calculus and optimization
strands.subtext: Partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, chain rule and constrained/unconstrained objectives. Derive tiny cases before consulting automatic differentiation.

strands.title: Probability and statistical reasoning
strands.subtext: Conditional probability, distributions, expectation, variance, joint variables, sampling, likelihood and intervals. Apply to evaluation and uncertainty.

strands.title: Run, measure and explain one model
strands.subtext: Model loading, tokens, prefill/decode, TTFT, throughput, latency percentiles, warm-up and basic memory accounting. Begin on supported local hardware.

strands.title: Serve efficiently on one device
strands.subtext: KV cache, scheduling, continuous batching, prefix reuse, quantization and measurement under load. Change one variable and retain quality checks.

strands.title: Kernels and runtime optimization
strands.subtext: Profiling, attention kernels, compilation, CUDA graphs, Triton and speculative decoding. NVIDIA-specific practice is optional pending hardware access.

strands.title: Distributed serving and specialization
strands.subtext: Parallelism, MoE, long context, disaggregated serving, multi-LoRA, multimodal and rollout workloads. Prioritize concepts before infrastructure.

strands.title: Production serving and economics
strands.subtext: Routing, lifecycle, scaling, observability, security and cost per useful completed task. Reliability and quality constrain throughput targets.

strands.title: Engine reading and research capstones
strands.subtext: Trace a request through an existing engine, then consider a deliberately tiny scheduling simulator or reproduction. Full engine construction is outside the first cycle.
